title: Admin - Comment Moderation - Approve & Publish Content - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Comment Moderation - Approve & Publish Content feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Admins to approve content making it publicly visible, with dashboard counts updating automatically and the action being logged with timestamp and admin name. Covers approval flow, visibility change, dashboard updates, audit logging, and edge cases.

testCases.title: Clicking 'Approve & Publish' updates status to Approved
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A moderation item with pending status (Needs Review, Ready to Approve) exists.
steps: Find a card with pending status
expectedResults: The status badge changes to 'Approved'
The change is immediate (no page refresh required)
A success notification may be displayed
The card reflects the new approved state
testCases.postconditions: Content status is updated to Approved

testCases.title: Approved content becomes publicly visible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content has just been approved.
steps: Open a new browser/incognito window as a regular user
Navigate to the product page where the content should appear
Observe if the approved content is visible
expectedResults: The approved content (review/query/response) is now publicly visible
Regular users can see the content on the relevant product page
The content displays correctly (author, text, date)
No admin-only information is exposed to public users
testCases.postconditions: Approved content is confirmed publicly visible

testCases.title: Dashboard counts update automatically after approval
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Dashboard with moderation counts is visible.
steps: Note the current pending count on the dashboard/moderation page
expectedResults: The pending count decreases by 1 after approval
The approved count increases by 1
The count update is automatic (no manual refresh needed)
The total count remains consistent

testCases.title: Action is logged with timestamp
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content has been approved.
steps: Observe the card or action log for timestamp
expectedResults: The approval action is logged with a timestamp
The timestamp shows the date and time of the approval
The timestamp is in a recognizable format
The timestamp is accurate (matches current time)

testCases.title: Action is logged with admin name
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin (pv@mailto.plus). Content has been approved.
steps: Observe the card or action log for admin name
Verify the admin name/email is recorded
expectedResults: The approval action is logged with the admin's name or email
The logged admin matches the currently logged-in user (e.g., 'pv@mailto.plus')
The admin name is automatically recorded by the system
The log provides accountability for the decision
testCases.postconditions: Admin name is confirmed logged with the action

testCases.title: Approve button is available on pending items
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Pending moderation items exist.
steps: Find cards with pending status (Needs Review, Ready to Approve, Vendor Flagged)
expectedResults: An 'Approve' or 'Approve & Publish' button is visible on pending cards
The button is clickable and not disabled
The button is clearly labeled
testCases.postconditions: Approve button is confirmed available on pending items

testCases.title: Approve button is NOT available on already-approved items
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Already-approved items exist.
steps: Observe the available actions on approved cards
expectedResults: Already-approved items do NOT show an 'Approve' button
OR the button is disabled/greyed out
The admin cannot re-approve already approved content
This prevents duplicate actions

testCases.title: Approved item moves out of Pending filter
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Pending filter is active.
steps: Note the items in the list
Approve one of the pending items
expectedResults: After approval, the item disappears from the Pending filter view
The item now appears in the 'Approved' filter view
The pending count decreases
The transition is smooth and immediate
testCases.postconditions: Approved item is moved to correct filter

testCases.title: Approval persists after page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content has been approved.
expectedResults: After refresh, the item still shows 'Approved' status
The approval is persisted to the backend
No data loss occurs on refresh
The action log (timestamp, admin) is still recorded

testCases.title: Multiple items can be approved sequentially
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Multiple pending items exist.
expectedResults: Each approval completes successfully
Dashboard counts update correctly after each approval
No errors occur during sequential approvals
Each action is logged independently with correct timestamp and admin

testCases.title: Approval failure shows error notification
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. API is configured to fail on approval.
steps: Attempt to approve a pending item (with API failure simulated)
expectedResults: An error notification is displayed (e.g., 'Failed to approve. Please try again.')
The item remains in its original pending status
No partial state change occurs
The admin can retry the action
